title: Workspace nuggets — fork, combine, and query inherited work
description: Standalone design decision for composing your three sources. All source facts, proposed behavior, tradeoffs and open decisions are contained in the questions and choices. Choose ONE primary approach in each question; choices are checkboxes, so combinations need an explanation in Additional notes. Modifiers in question 3 may be combined. No workspace is being created by attaching this form.

allowCodeFileChanges.label: Implement the selected design and chosen local workspace creation after this response
allowCodeFileChanges.description: Leave unchecked to continue design only. Checked permits nugs code changes and the creation scope selected below; copying/importing source data or publishing source Git objects must follow your selected choices rather than being implied by an association.

questions.title: 1. When we fork or combine workspaces, should inherited data stay with its sources or become new copies?
questions.description:
GOAL: Create a new workspace that can continue this workspace's work while using context from /var/tmp/vibe-kanban/worktrees/afff-github-ultimate and https://github.com/mickmister/gh-agentic-workflows. Combining context, materializing code, and merging task databases are separate operations. Associating two workspaces must not accidentally treat them as one task collection.

CURRENT SOURCES, inspected 2026-11-05: (A) This workspace is vk-46e5-vd-multi-instanc, local root /var/tmp/vibe-kanban/worktrees/46e5-vd-multi-instanc, with two repositories: vibe-dashboard/vibe-dashboard at 1f71008a99a42a68db379d567a96c01d01dc2428 and local workspace-nuggets at d516c4054458c1e5d817bbeb30facc49c0a4abce. Both use branch vk/46e5-vd-multi-instanc. Both working trees were clean. Its ONE workspace Beads collection has project ID a5544cff-ba4b-41e5-b3e0-08f4c831b4d3 and lives behind the root .beads/redirect in persisted workspace storage. Its native remote is configured, but no refs/dolt data is published. Its documents are published to private mickmister/workspace-storage under refs/documents/vk-46e5-vd-multi-instanc, currently commit 6afec7427b2c4c49da984fab6b51605897dc5fbc. That published manifest still records workspace-nuggets at 814609c, not the newer local d516c40; composition must distinguish published snapshots from newly observed local work.

(B) The second workspace is /var/tmp/vibe-kanban/worktrees/afff-github-ultimate, VD ID afff5e62-b0b0-4bd8-b432-5b645d2086c7. It contains mickmister/github-ultimate, a Chrome extension/CLI for GitHub decision forms, saved workflow context and bead progress. Local branch vk/afff-github-ultimate is clean at 712fce7cdf54d68c27f60ae3efa60e29d7fd3768; GitHub advertises that branch at a DIFFERENT commit, 4d9f57bab40a65ca80b492cdbd2d72cdc2117980. A remote branch name alone therefore does not reproduce the observed local tip. Its separate root-redirected Beads collection has project ID 9722db54-d4ca-4fda-b07d-acbf4cb09073, also database/prefix task, with no native remote configured and no-push=true. No published nugs manifest for this workspace was found in our storage repo.

(C) mickmister/gh-agentic-workflows is a public GitHub project using GitHub Issues, not Beads. Its observed default branch is feat/qrspi-resumable-workflow-poc at 506b1f14671dc2e4927bc1695603a59f9de0b8e5, also PR #1 against master. Relevant open issues include #2 orchestration, #6 portable workspace protocol, #7 feedback/MCP, and #8 artifact-driven resume. This source should be representable as an external project/provider association without inventing a Beads database or claiming it already has a nugs workspace.

MINIMAL PAPER TRAIL: The new manifest can own its repo bindings and task collection while recording associations with relation (forked_from, combined_from, or context_from), source kind, storage/project locator, readable workspace slug where present, exact source manifest/component revisions where available, and local/published/unavailable coverage. Source-native IDs remain qualified by Beads collection or GitHub repository. The same source listed twice is one identity with multiple provenance paths, not duplicated work. Branch slugs stay the human-facing handles; a bare branch name or task-1 is not a globally unique source identity.

Architecture of the recommended split:
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  N[New workspace manifest] --> O[Own repo bindings and fresh workspace Beads]
  N --> A[Association to current workspace snapshot]
  N --> B[Association to github-ultimate workspace snapshot]
  N --> C[Association to gh-agentic-workflows GitHub project]
  A --> R[Source-owned resources and task identities]
  B --> R
  C --> G[GitHub issue identities]
```

RETENTION TRADEOFF: A recorded hash is an audit reference, not a backup guarantee. In one Git storage repo, dedicated retained refs can keep referenced Git objects reachable without logically copying every document; across remotes or for unpublished/local data, objects must be captured or the source must remain accessible. Native Beads snapshot recovery must use compatible Dolt capabilities; a JSONL projection is not full database/history recovery. Git's byte deduplication also means logical copying is not necessarily equal to duplicating every byte. Select ONE primary ownership model below.

choices.label: Primary: pinned associations, fresh target tasks, selective copying
choices.description: Leave inherited docs/tasks owned by their source. Pin the observed source manifests/component versions and preserve their required storage objects where supported. Give the new workspace its own Beads collection and documents. An agent can explicitly promote a selected document or create a target follow-up linked to an older task; record copied_from/source version, and leave the original unchanged. Existing GitHub Issues stay authoritative in GitHub. Pros: small paper-trail-first design, reproducible context, no competing task authorities, source history remains queryable. Cons: complete availability still requires publishing/retaining currently local Beads and source objects; references alone cannot satisfy offline recovery. Parent updates require an explicit association refresh, and copied resources can subsequently diverge.
choices.is_recommended_reason: Preserves per-workspace Beads ownership while letting agents reuse older work. It makes composition a provenance operation first, without pretending independent databases have been merged.

choices.label: Primary: leave everything in place and follow live sources
choices.description: The new manifest records source locators and observed revisions for the paper trail, but normal queries follow each source's current head. New work can still have a fresh target task collection. Pros: least copying and retention machinery, freshest source task state, easy same-machine experimentation. Cons: context changes between runs; edits/deletions at a source affect the new workspace's view; parent outages or removal make inherited content unavailable. An observed old hash must not be presented as the version of a newly fetched live resource. This is association, not an isolated fork or portable archive.

choices.label: Primary: copy full source snapshots into the new workspace
choices.description: Capture supported source documents and separate Beads snapshots into target-controlled storage, preserving original identities and versions as provenance. Use a fresh writable target Beads collection; source snapshots remain distinct archives unless explicitly imported. For GitHub, copy selected issue/comment observations with provider IDs, timestamps and coverage, while distinguishing archived state from current issue state. Pros: stronger independence from parent availability and cleanup; straightforward historical/offline browsing once all dependencies are captured. Cons: more acquisition, retention and fidelity work; stale copies need explicit refresh; snapshotting GitHub does not capture unselected issues, undiscovered links, or all future updates. Forking a copied Beads database into a writable collection needs explicit new identity/lineage; two writable copies must not claim to be the same collection by accident.

choices.label: Primary: reuse a parent's writable Beads collection
choices.description: Attach the new workspace to one selected parent's actual Beads collection instead of creating its own. Other sources remain associations. Pros: existing task edits, comments and closures are immediately shared, with little copy/import work. Cons: this revises our per-workspace-isolated ownership rule; the new workspace is another attachment to the same task authority, not a task-data fork. Deleting/closing or changing tasks affects the parent. It cannot make two independent collections into one merely by adding redirects. Specify the primary shared collection in Additional notes if you choose this exception.

choices.label: Primary: import source tasks into one unified target collection
choices.description: Create a target-owned task collection and explicitly migrate selected tasks from the two Beads collections, optionally translating selected GitHub Issues if specified. Pros: one writable local backlog and uniform query surface. Cons: this is a data migration, not just a paper trail: task prefixes/IDs can collide; comments, dependencies, labels, metadata, forms and source links need mapping; historical/native identity and later write-back must be defined. Independently initialized Dolt databases are not safely combined by a blind pull/merge, and timestamp-based JSONL import is not replica reconciliation. Keep the source-to-target mapping and import coverage visible; source issues should not be automatically closed or rerouted. This is the largest first implementation.

questions.title: 2. How should CLI/MCP agents discover associated work, query it, and choose where edits go?
questions.description:
EXISTING IMPLEMENTATION: nugs currently has shared Go CLI/stdio MCP operations for workspace manifests and document list/read/upsert, centralized machine config at ~/.config/nugs/config.json, branch-slug workspace defaults, expected-version checks, clean native Git reconciliation, and native workspace Beads configuration/inspection. It does NOT yet implement workspace associations, cross-workspace resource/task queries, GitHub issue ingestion, source checkout materialization, or OpenCode conversation ingestion. New command names below are proposed, not existing features. Beads task operations remain native bd in each workspace's root context; GitHub task operations remain provider operations. No daemon is needed just to read explicit association metadata.

PROPOSED QUERY CONTRACT: workspace inspect returns owned resources plus association descriptors and availability/freshness. Proposed related/resources/tasks list and resource/task read operations accept an explicit source/scope and revision; CLI and MCP call the same operations. Every result includes its source locator, provider/collection identity, resource version, observation time and owned-versus-inherited status. A Beads task is identified by (collection ID, issue ID); a GitHub issue by (repository identity, issue number); a document by (workspace locator, resource identity, version). Both local Beads databases use the prefix task, so IDs/titles must never be globally deduplicated.

PINNED VS LIVE: Under a pinned model, ordinary inherited queries read the associated versions. Asking for latest reports the new version/diff separately, and refresh advances the target association with an expected-version update; it does not silently change the source. A live model instead reports the actual source version on every fetch. A GitHub issue is mutable: record the observed body/comment revisions or fetch time/coverage, rather than calling a URL alone an immutable snapshot. Missing Beads publication, unavailable local paths, permission failures and incomplete GitHub pagination appear as explicit unavailable/partial coverage, never zero tasks. Data of different kinds may have different observation times; there is no invented atomic snapshot across GitHub, documents and Beads.

WORKING ON OLDER WORK: Reading inherited tasks does not select their write destination. An agent may deliberately switch to a parent workspace/provider and use that owner's version-checked operations, or create a target-owned follow-up/promotion linked to it. Responses should state which source was read or changed. There should be no automatic upstream write-back merely because a resource was listed through the new workspace. This is explicit tool targeting, not a required human approval step for every ordinary edit. Historical forms/answers are context, not newly submitted questions or executable routing instructions in the target.

BOUNDED DISCOVERY: A manifest graph can have shared ancestors and context-link cycles. Keep derivation ancestry acyclic, use visited identities to handle other associations, and default to one association hop with explicit broader traversal. Do not recursively dump every transcript or all task bodies into an agent prompt. Source git histories remain separate even when their context is presented together.

REAL DESIGN DIFFERENCE TO SURFACE: gh-agentic-workflows issue #6 currently proposes an S3 workspace protocol and a fenced active executor; the current nugs decisions are Git-first and native clean reconciliation. Linking the sources should expose both decisions with provenance, not silently assert that the two designs are already unified. Select ONE primary discovery/query behavior.

choices.label: Primary: automatic related-source overview, explicit bounded drill-down
choices.description: An ordinary workspace inspection shows its own resources and a concise one-hop list of related workspaces/projects, pin/live policy, task providers, source revisions and availability. An agent can search/list tasks or read a particular resource across selected associated sources, with provenance on every result. Bodies and deep history are fetched only for the selected query. Current-workspace writes stay local; explicit source/provider targeting permits deliberate parent edits. Pros: agents discover prior work without guessing paths or remembering old workspace IDs; avoids context floods and accidental write destinations. Cons: requires provider-aware readers and a clear partial-results contract; searchable fields depend on available snapshots/providers rather than magic universal search.
choices.is_recommended_reason: Directly provides the discoverability you asked for while keeping current tasks, inherited evidence and source-native edits understandable.

choices.label: Primary: associations are links; agents switch sources explicitly
choices.description: Inspection lists related source descriptors only. Agents choose a workspace/provider and then run its ordinary list/read/search tools; there is no federated task or document search initially. Pros: smallest implementation and easiest provenance/write targeting; can reuse native bd and gh immediately where sources are available. Cons: more tool calls, more chance an agent misses relevant prior work, and no single combined task view. This can be an incremental first step toward the recommended overview/search behavior.

choices.label: Primary: show a combined inherited resource/task view by default
choices.description: Normal lists include owned and inherited resources automatically, with source-qualified identities and scope filters. Updates must still name the owner or explicitly copy-on-write into the target; a virtual combined list does not itself merge Beads databases or convert GitHub Issues. Pros: very ergonomic for an agent exploring all related work. Cons: naming collisions, duplicate presentation through multiple ancestry paths, provider differences and freshness are more visible design problems; agents may mistake historical or inherited tasks for the current backlog unless labels are excellent. Limit traversal depth and result budgets explicitly.

choices.label: Primary: eagerly gather related history and build a combined local index
choices.description: Fetch associated workspaces/projects recursively within an explicit budget and build a disposable local search index over supported resources. Pros: richer repeated search and potential offline queries after acquisition. Cons: substantially more ingestion, freshness, retention and indexing work; broad or cyclic associations can grow without bound; a local index must disclose missing sources and exact captured revisions. It cannot reconstruct unpublished Beads, absent Git objects or unrecorded conversations. Select this only if comprehensive repeated search is a first-slice requirement rather than a later expansion.

questions.title: 3. What should the first implementation actually create, and how portable must this specific combination be?
questions.description:
PROPOSED MEMBERSHIP, subject to your answer: four repository bindings in the new workspace—vibe-dashboard/vibe-dashboard and workspace-nuggets from the current workspace, mickmister/github-ultimate from the afff workspace, and mickmister/gh-agentic-workflows from GitHub. The two local workspace associations preserve their separate Beads identities; gh-agentic-workflows is an external GitHub project/task provider, not a synthetic Beads collection. The same current workspace mentioned more than once in the request is not duplicated. Each repository can start a new target branch from its own selected source commit; composing a multi-repo workspace does not merge unrelated Git histories or require one common base branch.

CAPTURE CHOICE MATTERS NOW: workspace-nuggets has no source remote. The VD workspace branch was not advertised by its origin. github-ultimate's local and advertised remote tips differ. The published nugs manifest lags current local code. Thus use newly observed local tips for a local continuation if selected, or explicitly choose published tips instead; do not quietly replace local work with a remote branch head. GitHub's observed gh-agentic-workflows branch is feat/qrspi-resumable-workflow-poc at 506b1f14671dc2e4927bc1695603a59f9de0b8e5, not an assumed master checkout. Source states must be re-observed when creation actually runs because these inspections can become stale. Both local working trees were clean at observation, but creation must report any newly dirty/untracked state and apply the chosen capture policy.

BEADS AVAILABILITY: Current and afff workspace collections remain on this machine; a reference to refs/dolt cannot fetch them until supported publication/snapshot capture actually occurs. Current origin is configured, afff has no origin, and mickmister/workspace-storage currently has custom document refs but no ordinary branch. Native Dolt Git transport requires an ordinary initial branch/commit before its first push. Bootstrap of that selected data repository and source snapshot recovery tests are real work if remote/offline Beads portability is selected. Do not initialize repository-based Beads or combine the two parent collections by a raw Dolt merge.

ASSUMPTIONS YOU CAN VETO IN NOTES: New workspace gets a new readable branch slug, its own root-level Beads attachment and separate repo directories; source workspaces remain independently usable. Local attachment metadata records whether nugs created/manages a checkout or it is externally managed by VD. No competing worktree manager changes another tool's checkout. Machine-local paths are hints for current-machine acquisition, not portable identities. We can create independent local clones from existing Git objects for unpublished commits; same-machine Git worktrees are faster but share object storage and lifetime with their source repo. The target workspace name/root and any different source branch selection belong in Additional notes. Existing Git-first storage remains the initial backend; association does not implicitly adopt issue #6's S3/executor design.

Select ONE Primary below. Optional Modifiers refine capture behavior and can be combined where consistent. Data ownership follows question 1 and agent visibility follows question 2; this question chooses implementation/materialization scope.

choices.label: Primary: create the combined local workspace from observed work
choices.description: Implement association manifests and the selected query behavior, then create a new local workspace with the four repo bindings at freshly verified local/GitHub commits and a fresh target-owned Beads collection (unless you selected the shared-collection exception). Use separate target branches/checkouts and retain source provenance. Existing local objects can supply unpublished source commits without pushing source branches. Use source-owned or retained context according to question 1, reporting any source that is still local-only. Pros: delivers a workspace you can work in soon using all current local work. Cons: not yet a guarantee that a different machine can recreate every repo/task snapshot; introduces local materialization and checkout-ownership handling beyond today's manifest-only CLI.
choices.is_recommended_reason: Matches your concrete next workspace while letting us validate composition locally before requiring every unpublished source to become remotely reconstructable.

choices.label: Primary: implement associations and queries before checkout creation
choices.description: Create the new workspace's manifest/association identity and selected resource/task browsing operations first. Leave source checkouts where they are and explicitly attach externally managed paths if needed; postpone cloning/materializing a complete new code workspace. Pros: smallest paper-trail-first slice, quick validation of discovery/provenance and GitHub task-source representation. Cons: does not yet fulfill a fully independent combined checkout; agents still switch to or attach existing source paths to edit code, with those source ownership rules.

choices.label: Primary: require full reconstruction on another machine immediately
choices.description: Before declaring creation complete, ensure selected source commits, chosen inherited documents and supported Beads snapshots are retained in accessible storage, then reconstruct the new workspace without source-local paths. Unpublished Git objects need explicit bundles/copies or a source remote; native Beads requires the data-repo bootstrap and verified recovery; GitHub snapshots need declared issue/comment coverage. Pros: genuine portability and independence from this machine. Cons: larger first build, more acquisition/publication and retention semantics, and blockers cannot be hidden behind association metadata. Provider-backed live issues still require provider access unless included in the selected snapshot coverage.

choices.label: Modifier: explicitly capture dirty/untracked source work if found
choices.description: If sources change before creation, preserve selected working-tree changes as a separately labeled snapshot/patch with provenance and coverage, including allowed untracked content. Keep source branches untouched rather than silently committing them. Pros: continuation can include current uncommitted work. Cons: needs inclusion/exclusion rules and recovery tests; it must not claim omitted files were preserved. Without this modifier, use committed tips and report newly dirty sources before claiming all work was captured.

choices.label: Modifier: retain unpublished source Git objects in private nuggets storage
choices.description: Publish explicitly selected Git bundles/object snapshots to the private storage backend with repository identity, commit and recovery receipts, enabling later reconstruction even for workspace-nuggets with no origin. Pros: preserves current source work without inventing a code remote or moving its source branch. Cons: adds code-object artifact handling and storage/lifetime dependencies; a commit pointer alone is not sufficient. This is distinct from ordinary nugget document publication.

choices.label: Modifier: retain selected GitHub issue/comment snapshots too
choices.description: Capture an explicit issue set and its observed comments/revisions for historical/offline context while retaining native GitHub identities and links. Pros: past discussion remains usable if it changes or becomes unavailable later. Cons: pagination, timestamps, selection and missing attachments must be recorded; this is an archive, not automatic conversion into target Beads or a promise to capture every issue. Specify issue selection in Additional notes; the observed related issues include #2, #6, #7 and #8.

questions.title: Additional notes — target workspace and overrides
questions.description: Master notes field. Give the new workspace/branch slug and desired local destination root (or ask me to propose them), any repository to exclude, source branch/SHA overrides, and exceptions to the selected data/query policy. If choosing shared tasks, identify the exact parent collection; if choosing task import, state GitHub-to-Beads scope and desired write-back behavior. If selecting issue snapshots, name the issue set. Explain any combination of multiple Primary choices. The current source facts and limitations are already in the questions, so no external document is required to answer.
